# External published nonlinear DAG learners vs our methods: edge-function accuracy

Status: committed BEFORE any run on the evaluation seeds. Code that existed at commit time: extlib.py (external methods), ext_bench.py (driver). Only debug seeds (9001, one dataset at d=10 and d=20, never used again) were run to find bugs; they changed two settings, disclosed in section 7.

## 1. Question
Our paper compares only variants of the SPADE family. No published nonlinear DAG-learning paper evaluates the recovered edge functions (amplitude/shape) or interventional effects; they report SHD/AUROC. We score external learners on the same edge-function and do-effect metrics as ours, on identical datasets, to see whether the SPADE-family conclusions survive an outside comparison.

## 2. Data
iSCM generator `gen_full` of research/replication/bench.py (unchanged, imported read-only), mechanism family m1, n = 1000, ER mean degree 2, fresh seeds 4000-4009 (never used before). Cells: E1 d=10 uniform noise, E2 d=20 uniform, E3 d=10 Laplace; 10 datasets each (30 total). Method seed 0 for every method. d <= 20 because the external learners do not scale (DAGMA-MLP, GraN-DAG, NOTEARS-MLP take minutes at d=20; we do not push further under a 1-core budget). A Sachs-based semi-synthetic arm is NOT added: research/semisyn/ has no committed generator or results at the time of writing.
Screening note: our SSC/SSA/SSR/BASILWs use `screen_mask(K=15)`. At d=10 (9 candidate causes per node) it keeps all candidates (vacuous). At d=20 (19 candidates) it drops only the 4 lowest ExtraTrees-ranked causes per node (mild, not vacuous). The external methods have no screening.

## 3. Methods (each is reported as RUN or COULD NOT RUN with a reason in README_results.md)
Ours (run through bench.run_method of research/replication unchanged; SSA = the branch of research/adaptive/bench.py, code copied): SSC (SPADE-scaled), SSA (adaptive), SSR_k1.5 (top 1.5 d edges refit), BASILWs, GAM-ridge (reference baseline, spline ridge GAM from the G2 benchmark; included for context, not a SPADE variant).
External / published:
1. NOTEARS-MLP (repo): the PyTorch re-implementation in scripts/instantaneous_dag_benchmark.py (Adam, 600 epochs, hidden 10, l1 on first layer, no l2 on the second layer). NOT the original code.
2. NOTEARS-MLP-gc: gcastle 1.0.4 `NotearsNonlinear` (port of the original: L-BFGS-B, l1 on fc1, l2 on all weights, lambda1 = lambda2 = 0.01, hidden 10).
3. DAGMA-nonlinear: dagma 1.1.1 `DagmaNonlinear` with the repo call (dims [d,10,1], lambda1 .02, lambda2 .005, T=4, warm_iter 4000, max_iter 8000, default lr). Note the library defaults use 10x more iterations.
4. DCE-like: the same fitted DAGMA-MLP re-scored by a derivative-based edge strength, RMS over data of d f_e / d x_c. dagma 1.1.1 does not expose Dagma-DCE (Waxman et al. 2024), whose DCE enters the training objective; this is a post-hoc score on a DAGMA-nonlinear fit, NOT Dagma-DCE. Curves and do-effects are identical to DAGMA-nonlinear; only S and the own graph differ.
5. GraN-DAG: gcastle 1.0.4 `GraNDAG` defaults (iterations 10000, 2 hidden layers of 10, leaky ReLU), no CAM pruning (gcastle does not implement it).
6. CAM-like (own Python implementation, NOT the original R CAM): additive models of cubic B-spline terms (6 quantile knots, 8 basis functions per term) fitted by OLS; greedy forward edge addition (CAM's IncEdge idea) with gain = (n/2) log(RSS_old/RSS_new) - 0.5 log(n) * 8, stop when no feasible acyclic addition has positive gain; then per-node F-test pruning of every parent term at p < 0.001 (single pass, no multiplicity correction).
7. NAM-SSC and NAM-SSR_k1.5 (NAM-parameterised variants of the SPADE family, NOT the original NAM): x_e = b_e + sum_c f_ec(x_c), each f_ec a one-hidden-layer tanh MLP with 16 units (no ExU units, no feature dropout), same objective as the spline SPADE (MSE + lg * sum of group norms + augmented-Lagrangian NOTEARS acyclicity on the group-norm matrix, lg = min(0.01, 0.2/d), 400 full-batch Adam epochs, lr 1e-2, ALM update every 50 epochs), same screening mask as SSC, group norm = sqrt(11) * RMS(f_ec). NAM-SSR_k1.5 refits unpenalised on the top 1.5 d edges of NAM-SSC, exactly as SSR does for SSC. Hyperparameters were not tuned.
COULD NOT RUN (decided in advance, no attempt): the original R CAM (no R here), original Dagma-DCE training, KAN-based Granger methods (time-series, different task), SCORE/NoGAM (order methods without edge functions, structure only, already in earlier tables).

## 4. What is extracted and how each method is scored
Data are z-scored. For every TRUE edge (c -> e) we need phi_ce on the data points of x_c, centered; truth is f_ce(x_c)/sd_e centered (as in bench.edge_curve_metrics).
Curve extraction: additive models (CAM-like, NAM variants, GAM-ridge, our spline models) give phi_ce directly. For MLP methods: partial dependence. Grid of 41 quantiles of x_c; for each grid value v, replace column c by v in a fixed random subsample of 300 observed rows, average the model output of node e; linear interpolation to the data points of x_c. All other inputs keep their observed values. The truth is additive, so partial dependence targets the right object even though the MLPs are not additive.
Three scoring rules, all reported for every arm where defined (statistic = per-dataset mean over true edges, then mean over datasets):
- RAW (no selection): the curve of the fitted model as is (all edges the model has). This is how all earlier SPADE results were scored. GraN-DAG removes edges during training, so RAW = OWN for it; CAM-like RAW uses the forward-search graph before pruning.
- OWN (the method's own thresholded graph; defined for external methods and for SSR, BASILWs; NOT defined for SSC, SSA, GAM-ridge, NAM-SSC/NAM-SSR which have no selection step): a true edge that is not selected gets curve 0, i.e. NRMSE 1, R2 0, slope 0. Own graphs: NOTEARS-MLP (both) and DAGMA-nonlinear: W >= 0.3 (the library convention); DCE-like: strength >= 0.1 (fixed a priori, not tuned; true standardized effects have derivatives of order 0.3-1); GraN-DAG: its final adjacency; CAM-like: after pruning; SSR: nonzero refit importance (its top 1.5 d edges); BASILWs: posterior inclusion probability > 0.5. A cyclic own graph is made acyclic by removing the weakest edge of a cycle until acyclic.
- TOPK (oracle count): select the k = number of true edges highest entries of the method's edge-score matrix S (zero scores are never selected); missed true edges score NRMSE 1, R2 0, slope 0. This gives every method the true edge count (oracle information), so it is a reference, not a deployable rule. It is applied identically to our arms. PRIMARY RULE for the verdicts: TOPK, because it puts all arms on equal footing; OWN and RAW are secondary.
Edge scores S [cause, effect]: ours as in bench (spline importance; BASILWs posterior probability); NOTEARS-MLP and DAGMA: first-layer weight norm; DCE-like: RMS derivative; GraN-DAG: gcastle path-weight adjacency; CAM-like: -log10 p of the term F-test for edges in the forward graph, 0 otherwise (heavily tied); NAM: std of f_ec. Directed AUROC, skeleton AUROC, orientation accuracy from bench.metrics. Tied binary scores are expected to give AUROC near the binary balanced accuracy.
Reported metrics: edge NRMSE (primary), curve R2 (mean over true edges), median calibration slope, AUROC, orientation, own-graph precision/recall counts, do-effect NRMSE for up to 20 direct and 20 indirect true pairs (do_error of research/replication/docalc.py, same pairs for all methods, pairs with std(truth)<0.05 skipped and counted), fit time.
Do-effect adapter: same propagation code as docalc.make_learned with a callable node predictor: x_c := v, descendants in the learned topological order are recomputed as prediction(parents) + in-sample residual. External methods use their own (DAG-ified) graph: node predictor = the trained network/GAM with the inputs of non-parents removed (first-layer weights zeroed, no refit); order = topological order of the own graph. NAM variants use the same rule as our spline arms (source-peeling order on group norms, all earlier nodes with nonzero norm are parents). GAM-ridge has no do-effect (as in bench). DAGMA/DCE-like/NOTEARS do-effects therefore depend on the thresholded graph; this is the fixed rule.
Time: wall-clock of the fit only, one core shared with other jobs (noisy; medians reported). For ours: t_cost of bench (screen + fit [+ refit/MCMC/extract]); SSA: t_ss + refit; excludes metric and do code. DCE-like time = DAGMA fit + derivative extraction.

## 5. Statistics and verdict rules
"Our best arm" = the arm among {SSC, SSA, SSR_k1.5, BASILWs} with the lowest pooled mean TOPK NRMSE over the 30 datasets (chosen on the evaluation data; the external best arm is chosen the same way from the external list, so the selection is symmetric). Paired comparison per cell and pooled over 30 datasets: two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank, bootstrap 95% CI of the mean paired difference (10,000 resamples, seed 0, percentile), datasets better counts. Pooled results overstate evidence: E1 and E3 share the same 10 DAGs/mechanisms (same seeds, only noise differs).
Verdicts (pre-registered): an external arm TIES ours if |mean paired TOPK NRMSE difference| <= 0.03; it BEATS ours if it is lower by more than 0.03 with the CI excluding 0; ours beats it in the mirrored case. The same three-way verdict is given per cell and for the secondary rules, for AUROC (tie band 0.03), and for do-effects (tie band 0.05). No multiplicity correction beyond reporting all cells; 10 datasets per cell have limited power (about dz = 1 at 80 %).

## 6. Predictions (stated before seeing the results; no win is promised for our methods)
- CAM-like fits the true model class (additive, smooth, spline friendly) with an F-test pruner and no shrinkage. At d <= 20 with n = 1000 I expect it to be as good as or better than our best arm on edge NRMSE and AUROC (probability of at least a tie in 2 of 3 cells: about 65 %). It would count as "external method matches or beats ours" if its TOPK NRMSE is within 0.03 of or below our best arm in at least 2 of the 3 cells. Its weaknesses should be orientation (greedy, local) and the p-value pruner under Laplace noise.
- MLP methods (NOTEARS-MLP repo/gc, DAGMA-nonlinear, DCE-like, GraN-DAG): I expect them to be worse than ours on structure (AUROC / orientation near chance to 0.8) and on edge NRMSE (0.5-1.0 under TOPK because wrong or missed edges count 1), with DAGMA-nonlinear the best of them. If any of them reaches TOPK NRMSE within 0.03 of our best arm in a cell, that is reported as a tie/win for the external method.
- NAM-SSC should behave like SSC (shrunken amplitudes, NRMSE about 0.6-0.8, good AUROC); NAM-SSR like SSR (within about 0.05 of it). If NAM-SSR is clearly better than SSR (> 0.03), the spline parameterisation is not what drives accuracy in the SPADE-family, which would be reported.
- BASILWs vs SSR: at d <= 20 the earlier d=100 advantage of BASILWs over SSR may vanish or reverse (small d, few candidate edges); no prediction of superiority.
- Do-effects: CAM-like and SSR/SSA similar; MLP methods worse when the thresholded graph misses edges.

## 7. Limitations and disclosed deviations
- d <= 20, n = 1000, one mechanism family, iSCM only, 10 datasets per cell; nothing is concluded about larger d, other generators, real data.
- The iSCM generator is additive, so additive learners (CAM-like, NAM, ours) are matched to the truth, whereas MLP learners are not; this favors additive methods and is a property of the benchmark, not evidence about real data.
- Reimplementations (CAM-like, NAM variants, DCE-like) may differ from the originals in ways that matter; the repo NOTEARS-MLP differs from the original NOTEARS-MLP. gcastle versions are used as the reference code for NOTEARS-MLP-gc and GraN-DAG, with default hyperparameters; none of the external methods is tuned on this generator, while SPADE's lg rule and k=1.5 were chosen on earlier validation seeds of the same generator family. External methods are therefore at a possible disadvantage.
- Thresholds for OWN graphs (0.3, 0.1) are conventions fixed in advance; different thresholds change OWN, not RAW/TOPK.
- Debug-seed disclosure: a run on seed 9001 showed GraN-DAG with 2000 iterations (repo setting) returning an empty graph at d=20, so the gcastle default 10000 iterations is used; NAM lr 1e-2 was fixed before any run and not tuned. Results of the debug seeds are not used.
- Failures are reported (error column in the CSV), never dropped.
